name: Alien Gambit
summary: An aggressive gambit against the Caro-Kann: after 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Nf6 5.Ng5 h6 White plays 6.Nxf7!?, giving a knight for a pawn to pull Black's king into the open. White then develops quickly with Nf3, Bc4 or Bd3, castles and attacks along the e- and f-files. It is objectively dubious but very dangerous over the board. This small file is a frontend development fixture; the real repertoire lives in data/openings.
keyIdeas: 6.Nxf7 trades a knight for a pawn and the right of Black's king to castle.
The a2-g8 diagonal is the key attacking line: Bc4+ often comes with tempo.
Ne5+ is a recurring resource because no black pawn can chase the knight from e5.
Pile up on e6 with Re1 and Qe2 or Qf3: it is the pawn that holds Black's position together.
typicalPlans: Castle short, put a rook on e1 and attack e6.
Use Nh4 and Qf3 or Qh5+ to bring more pieces to the kingside.
commonMistakes: Attacking too slowly: if Black gets ...Kg8 and ...Nbd7 in, the extra piece decides.

lines.name: Main line: 7...Bf5 8.Bc4+
lines.description: Black develops the bishop actively. White checks on c4, castles and brings the rook to e1 to pile up on e6.
lines.evaluation: Objectively better for Black (a piece for a pawn), but White's attack is easy to play.

lines.name: 7...e6: the solid shell
lines.description: Black blocks the diagonal at once. White aims the bishop at h7 and jumps into e5 with check.
lines.evaluation: Black is better on material; White has long-term pressure on the exposed king.

lines.name: Trap: 7...Bg4? 8.Ne5+!
lines.description: Pinning the knight looks natural, but Ne5+ is check and attacks the bishop at the same time.
lines.evaluation: White regains the piece and keeps an extra pawn against an exposed king.
